runs.title: First map: open sessions, buffered clips, and local H3
runs.summary: First public research map separates the route types and preserves the main cost, hardware, and continuity limits.

runs.title: FastH3 local access, reality checked
runs.summary: FastH3 gained local Apple Silicon and DGX Spark paths, but the fastest stated local preview condition still requires about 23 wall seconds per output second.

runs.title: A broadcast can continue while FastH3 scenes hard-cut
runs.summary: Reactor’s current project documents a queue and paced RTMP broadcast, while its independently generated FastH3 clips do not retain subject, framing, or voice across boundaries.

runs.title: FastH3 autoplay is a setting, not a stream
runs.summary: Reactor’s current FastH3 contract defaults to black after a clip until a client plays the next one; an optional autoplay policy can advance ready clips but cannot supply a buffer or preserve the story.

runs.title: Four B200s do not clear FastH3’s documented 15-second deadline
runs.summary: Reactor’s current project documentation separates a roughly 15-second FastH3 build into about 15.5 seconds on four B200 GPUs and 12.9 seconds on eight; the update also records the current Director price and a local 5090 offline signal.

runs.title: A one-5090 FastH3 channel is a format claim, not a live-interaction claim
runs.summary: A new community project reports a continuous FastH3 channel on one RTX 5090, but its usable reading is condition-bound: 448×448 output, source-stated 22.1 fps, prequeued work, retimed motion, and distinct scenes.

runs.title: YoLive control-loop reality check
runs.summary: Yoroll’s provider-announced group vote route adds a public deployment shape; the cited four-second clip time is not a measured vote-to-screen result.

runs.title: An H3 video API is a route, not a live-video result
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service, while its named four-B300 full-H3 row returns about 8.7 seconds of output in about 87 seconds.

runs.title: FastH3 ComfyUI scope conflict
runs.summary: FastH3 8-Step V2 reached a current ComfyUI workflow, but FastVideo and ComfyUI disagree on first/last-frame support.

runs.title: A 5090 FastH3 run is a faster review loop, not live video
runs.summary: A platform-published FastH3 Preview v1 test reports 55 seconds for 15.08 seconds of 480×640 output and 126 seconds at 768×1024 on one RTX 5090, with a stated hot complete-MP4 boundary.

runs.title: FastH3 V2 scope recheck
runs.summary: A direct check of the exact FastVideo model card and the current official ComfyUI template left the FL2VA conflict unresolved; no new local performance or live-video evidence was found.

runs.title: FastH3 V2 has a native-canvas speed boundary
runs.summary: A detailed community Radeon report puts one FastH3 V2 768×1344, 243-frame run at 33 minutes 9 seconds; its stated sparse-attention threshold explains why smaller canvases may gain nothing. The result is a local-render lead, not live video.

runs.title: Dreamverse FastH3 profile: four-GPU chain, unmeasured capacity
runs.summary: FastVideo’s current README documents a frame-carried FastH3 Preview v1 profile and a cold readiness boundary; the pool treats it as an implementation lead, not a live result.

runs.title: Eight B300s clear FastH3’s complete-MP4 playback threshold
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni’s maintainer report says a warmed dedicated FastH3 T2VA profile returned 10.125 seconds of MP4 in 8.678–8.710 seconds on eight B300 GPUs; the public record keeps streaming, cold, queue, and raw-evidence limits visible.

runs.title: Two RTX 5090s can run full H3. The documented job still takes 8:38 for five seconds of video.
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni documents one two-RTX-5090 full-H3 T2VA capacity validation, with large host-RAM requirements and no live-performance claim.

runs.title: The H3 server can take first and last frames. vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client cannot send both.
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni’s current documentation separates the server’s two-keyframe and richer-reference capability from a current client limited to one FL2VA frame and constrained references.

runs.title: H3 can schedule between denoise steps. Its four-request test still took longer.
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni’s named two-H100 H3 test finds four simultaneous jobs slower under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode; the candidate also clarifies the selected FL2VA task path behind the two-RTX-5090 capacity record.

runs.title: ComfyUI H3 VAE speed has a stage boundary
runs.summary: Comfy Org reports a faster H3 VAE encode/decode round trip on an RTX 5090, but no full-generation or live-service timing.

runs.title: H3 long-video output is not a live H3 stream
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni v0.30.0 documents opt-in Ref2VA continuation, but its eight-B300 30.667-second example lacks full wall time and viewer-visible delivery evidence.

runs.title: Four H3 steps do not make every short clip real time
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni reports 11.7–11.8 seconds for a 4.4-second FastH3 clip on eight B300 GPUs; the whole response is slower than playback despite a fast denoiser.

runs.title: Vidu S2 documents live feed editing, not another H3 clip path
runs.summary: The provider documents RTC input and edited RTC/RTMP output at one credit per live second; end-to-end delay, sustained reliability and delivered cost remain unverified.

runs.title: Sol-H3 warm inference is not a live show
runs.summary: NVIDIA reports fast eight-B300 H3 inference with a four-forward adapter, while final encoding and continuous interaction remain unmeasured.

runs.title: TaoMate-H3 first playable chunk, not a live session
runs.summary: The project reports 17.287 seconds to a first playable benchmark chunk on eight H20s, while receiver-visible continuity and cost remain unmeasured.

runs.title: FastH3 on Hopper: a warm complete clip, not a show
runs.summary: An independent eight-H100 project reports a 14.375-second audio-video clip saved in 13.506 seconds; quality and viewer delivery remain unmeasured.

runs.title: H3 mask editing reached the server API before its ComfyUI client
runs.summary: vLLM-Omni supports request-scoped H3 mask editing in its video API; the dedicated ComfyUI client remained an open PR. Neither is measured live control.

runs.title: Griffin's fast face is not a complete call
runs.summary: Tavus reports full-duplex video with a 0.43-second component clock; NVIDIA benchmark event timing differs, and Griffin remains a selected-tester preview.

runs.title: RAVEN’s 24-GiB claim needs two separate test labels
runs.summary: The long test used H200 headroom and synthetic conditioning. A real full-size prompt on a physical 24-GiB card is not shown.

runs.title: Veda speeds an H3 clip, not a live stream
runs.summary: The project reports 130.1 seconds for 5.17 seconds of H3 output on a 5070; 7.1× is an attention-only figure.

runs.title: ShotStream: H200 model speed is not a public live client
runs.summary: Paper-reported near-playback multi-shot model throughput is separated from the released CSV-to-final-MP4 example and unmeasured viewer delivery.

runs.title: LiveAvatar: 45 FPS stream is not a finished conversation
runs.summary: Paper five-H100 throughput and first-frame clock are separated from its estimated delivered delay and an independent one-H200 offline job.

runs.title: Hallo-Live: model speed is not a live client
runs.summary: Two-H200 author throughput is separated from the current saved-MP4 command and approximately 60-GB default memory estimate.

runs.title: Scope has a live browser route; show readiness is still unproven
runs.summary: WebRTC client documentation is separated from one remote-beta operator record, paid-use license, cold start and rollover uncertainty.

runs.title: TeleFuser: a one-minute media replay took 79 seconds of session time
runs.summary: Four-H100 target compute above 16 FPS is separated from first client frame, callback cadence and full one-minute session time.

runs.title: StreamRender-H3 browser route: three clocks, no player-delay result
runs.summary: Released eight-GB200 racing integration separates diffusion, GPU RGB-ready and browser publication clocks; input-to-screen time and cost remain unknown.

runs.title: Waypoint-1.5 plays in a browser on one GPU. The world lasts seconds.
runs.summary: One-GPU browser route with local generation, remote delivery, cold compile and short coherent-scene boundaries.

runs.title: StreamForce: an unpaced change sat 13 seconds ahead of display in a local test
runs.summary: A released force-control demo measures how pacing reduces stale input, while network delay, scene life and cost remain unresolved.

runs.title: One RTX 5090 beats playback speed. The browser still waits for two clips.
runs.summary: A warm paired H3 result crosses playback speed, while the released HLS client still gates first playback on two finished clips and lacks a receiver response measurement.

runs.title: H3 can decode its first frame in 40 ms. Generation still sets the wait.
runs.summary: A new H3 VAE decoder removes the wait for future latents, but the reported 40 ms begins only after a latent exists; end-to-end viewer delay and cost remain unknown.
